reason: The text explicitly demonstrates that non-leaders possess and exercise agency. The Hebrew term 'ha'am' (העם - 'the people') appears repeatedly as the subject of active verbs: they go out (יָצְאוּ), they gather (לָֽקְטוּ), they attempt to gather on the Sabbath (יָצְאוּ מִן־ הָעָם לִלְקֹט), and they rest (וַיִּשְׁבְּתוּ הָעָם). Additionally, the text uses 'ish' (איש - 'each man') as an individual agent with the capacity to choose his actions ('אִישׁ תַּחְתָּיו - each man in his place'). The people collectively exercise agency in deciding whether to obey God's commandments regarding the Sabbath, even if that exercise involves disobedience. Leadership (Moses and God) is present, but agency clearly extends beyond leaders to the community and individuals.
